summary: Franklin Edgerton was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield, after studies at Cornell, Munich, and Jena. He was a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1913–1926) and Yale University (1926–1953).

Franz Altheim worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Goethe University Frankfurt (1921–1928), he held posts at Frankfurt (~1928–1943), Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg (~1943–1950), and the Free University of Berlin (~1950–1964).

Franz Aubrey Metcalf is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago. He served as an instructor at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 2002–2006).

Franz Bernhard was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctorate at Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt and his habilitation at Frankfurt. He served as professor at the University of Hamburg from 1966 to 1971.

Franz Boas was a linguist and anthropologist who studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, and Kiel, and under Wilhelm Wundt. He held posts at Clark University (~1889–1892), the American Museum of Natural History (1896–1900), and Columbia University (~1896–1942).

Franz Bopp was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Paris under Antoine-Léonard Chézy and Silvestre de Sacy, as well as in London and Göttingen. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1821 to 1867.

Franz Ferdinand Schwarz was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Graz from 1953 to 1958. He later served as a professor at the University of Graz from approximately 1978 to 1999.

Franz Heinrich Trithen was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp. He held posts at the British Museum (~1844–1848) and as professor of modern languages at Oxford University (~1848–1854).

Franz Kielhorn was an Indologist who studied at Göttingen, Breslau, Berlin, and under Adolf Stenzler and Theodor Benfey. He held chairs at Deccan College (1866–1881) and the University of Göttingen (1881).

Franz Simon Ferdinand Benary was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Bonn, Halle-Wittenberg, and Berlin under Franz Bopp. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin as a lecturer in 1829 and professor in theology starting in 1831.

Franz Xaver Erhard is a Tibetologist who earned master's degrees from the Free University of Berlin and Humboldt University of Berlin, and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Bonn (attested 2003).

Franz von Erdmann was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. After studying at the University of Rostock from 1813 to 1817, he held a post at Kazan Imperial University from approximately 1818 to 1845.

Franz-Karl Ehrhard is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his degrees at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He served as resident representative for the Nepal Research Centre and later as professor at the University of Munich (2001–2019).
François Grimal is an Indologist who held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and served as director at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2003).
François Gros was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lyon from 1951 to 1956. He served as Directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from approximately 1977 to 2002.
François Lachaud is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who held a professorial post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2008 and 2013).
Françoise Pommaret is a Tibetologist and historian who studied at the Sorbonne, INALCO, and the University of Paris. She has held posts at CNRS, INALCO, and the Royal University of Bhutan.

Françoise Robin is a Tibetologist who studied at INALCO under Heather Stoddard. She served as a director at the Collège de France (2009–2015) and held departmental leadership posts at INALCO between 2011 and 2014.

Fred Pfeil worked in Buddhist studies and other fields, studying at Amherst College and Stanford University. He taught at Stanford, Stephens College, Oregon State University, and Trinity College, Hartford (~1985–2005).

Freda Bedi was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at St Hugh's College (1929–1933) and under Mahasi Sayadaw (1952–1954). She founded the Young Lamas Home School and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling Nunnery.
